subject: FinPay — Post-call: data retention options & next steps
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Sam Turner <sam.turner@finpay.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: FinPay — Post-call: data retention options & next steps

Hi Sam,

Great to meet earlier — thanks for the product deep-dive. Per our conversation, I wanted to capture the key asks and proposed next steps so your team and Legal have a clear starting point.

Summary of FinPay requirements (as discussed):
- PII/data-minimization: do not persist cardholder-sensitive fields in any retrievable logs.
- 0-retention option for request/response content (customer requires no storage of prompt + output).
- Shortened operational logs: application-level logs (non-content) retained for max 7 days for debugging, unless a debug window is explicitly approved.
- Billing/usage metadata: token counts and billing metadata to be kept only as long as required for invoicing — proposed 30 days.
- Data residency: host inference in us-east-1 (preferred).

What Redwood can offer (initial proposals):
- API-level 0-retention mode: we can disable request/response content logging; however we retain minimal billing metadata (token counts, request timestamps) for 30 days to support invoicing and audit.
- Shortened logs: application/debug logs configurable to 7 days for your account; we can implement stricter controls in a dedicated environment.
- Private / Dedicated deployment: for full control (no shared logs, VPC, KMS integration) — will require contract & infra onboarding.

Attachments: DataRetentionMatrix.xlsx (matrix mapping each log type to proposed retention and protections).

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm that the definition of “0-retention” below matches FinPay’s ask: no storage of request/response content outside ephemeral memory used during inference. Minimal billing metadata retained for 30 days.
2) Legal to review and provide initial redlines to the DPA (I’ll attach a DPA draft once you confirm).
3) Security to confirm SOC2 artifacts & encryption controls (I’ve looped in our security lead in follow-ups).
4) If needed, we’ll scope a dedicated deployment and provide an estimated onboarding timeline/cost.

Can you confirm or correct the bullets above and let me know who on your side I should loop in for the DPA redlines?

Thanks,

Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182
[attachment: DataRetentionMatrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Sam Turner <sam.turner@finpay.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal@finpay.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FinPay — Post-call: data retention options & next steps

Camila — thanks for the recap and the fast follow-up. A few clarifying Qs from our side before Legal starts redlining: 

1) When you say “0-retention mode”, does that mean Redwood will not persist request/response content anywhere (logs, analytics, debug snapshots)? Or is content still written to ephemeral logs that could be recovered for debugging?
2) Is it possible to disable request/response logging per-route so we can keep it off for production but enable for staging only?
3) Billing metadata for 30 days is reasonable, but can you confirm what fields are included in that metadata (we need to confirm no PII fields are present in billing records).
4) Please share SOC 2 report or a summary of control mappings relevant to data handling and key management.

Legal Ops (cc’ed) — can you take a look at the attached matrix once Camila confirms and we’ll start a DPA redline pass.

Proposed timeline: we’re hoping to lock terms by end of month; is that feasible on your side?

Best,
Sam
Director, Platform Security | FinPay
sam.turner@finpay.com

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Sam Turner <sam.turner@finpay.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FinPay — Post-call: data retention options & next steps

Thanks Sam — great questions. Answers below and I’ve attached a draft DPA with some initial redlines for Legal to review.

Answers: 
- 0-retention mode: We can commit to not persisting request/response content in any persistent logs or analytics systems for FinPay production traffic. During inference the data exists only in memory and is not stored. For any debug session where content is captured, it requires a written debug request and will be timeboxed and audited.
- Per-route control: Yes — we support per-route logging flags. We can keep production routes at 0-retention and enable content logging for a staging/test route.
- Billing metadata fields: we retain only non-PII fields needed for billing: account_id, route_id, timestamp, token_counts, usage_cost. No raw prompt or response content is included.
- SOC2 / security artifacts: attaching a pointer to our security pack and SOC2 summary. Neha can provide the pack directly.

Attached: DPA_redlines_v2.pdf, DataRetentionMatrix.xlsx

Next steps here from Redwood:
1) Legal review DPA_redlines_v2.pdf (Sam/legal ops).
2) Security (Neha) to share SOC2 summary + KMS/crypto brief.
3) If Legal requires contract-level exception language, Rafael will draft the exhibit for the DPA.
4) Camila / Marissa to confirm commercial terms and dedicated onboarding estimate if required.

Links: HubSpot deal (DEAL-7382), DocuSign placeholder for later.

On timeline — we can target EOM for MSAs if legal review starts early next week.

Thanks,

Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[attachment: DPA_redlines_v2.pdf (pdf)]
[attachment: DataRetentionMatrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

Camila — please prioritize this. FinPay is a high-value payments prospect (DEAL-7382) and their ask is within scope for a contract exception with Legal/Security signoff. Rafael — can you review DPA_redlines_v2 and draft the exhibit language that explicitly: (a) prohibits persistence of request/response content, (b) permits operator-run debug captures only with written FinPay approval and a max 72-hour retention window, and (c) confirms billing metadata fields retained for 30 days only.

Neha — please send SOC2 summary and confirm KMS integration options for a dedicated deployment.

Thanks — Marissa

Marissa Cole

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Sam Turner <sam.turner@finpay.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal@finpay.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 10:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FinPay — Post-call: data retention options & next steps

Sam / Camila — I reviewed DPA_redlines_v2.pdf and drafted an exhibit that should cover FinPay’s requirements. High level: 
- We’ll include a DPA exhibit stating Redwood will not persist request/response content for production traffic ("No Content Persistence").
- Operator debug captures are permitted only with documented written approval from FinPay and will be retained no longer than 72 hours; all captures will be logged in an audit trail.
- Billing metadata will be limited to account_id, route_id, timestamp, token_counts and stored for 30 days for invoicing/audit; no PII fields will be present.
- For customers requiring cryptographic separation and dedicated KMS, we recommend a Dedicated deployment; I’ve included language for optional migration in the exhibit.

I’ve attached the redlined DPA (DPA_Redlines_Final.pdf) for Legal Ops to route to FinPay. If that looks good, we can prepare an execution packet and I’ll coordinate with FinPay Legal on any final wording.

Regards,
Rafael Mendes
Counsel, Redwood Inference
[attachment: DPA_Redlines_Final.pdf (pdf)]
